market_holds: Spot $2.2151 (sealed baseline, 2026-11-13 18:14 UTC). It is down 14.1% over 5 sessions and 15.5% over 20, 12.6% above the 52-week low, with 67% annualised realised volatility. There is no option market, so the usual move comes from the last five prints: median 13.26%, and 4 of 5 went down (-7.8, -17.0, +28.2, -12.0, -13.3). 18,131,385 shares are outstanding after the FanEngine issue closed on 2026-10-26 (13D filings of 2026-11-04/06/09), which gives a market cap of about $40m. Consensus per the Earnings Whispers preview of 2026-11-08 is Q3 revenue about $21.3m and EPS -$0.16, with a full-year consensus of $78.8m, below the company's guide. That guide was $85-90m 'pro forma' (shareholder letter 2026-06-04, reiterated 2026-08-10) and was restated at FanEngine's close on 2026-10-26 as '$85+ million pro forma', with FanEngine named as a contributor. 2027 guidance is above $150m revenue and above $30m adj. EBITDA. So the street already discounts management's guide. At Q2 the company held 15,080 ETH plus about $12.1m of ETH-backed current promissory notes (margin call and 120% liquidation terms in the Q2 10-Q), $2.1m of cash and a going-concern paragraph. ETH was about $1,954 on 2026-11-13, down 19% in a month and about 28% below its 2026-09-30 level of about $2,705. The stock's 5- and 20-day run-in tracks ETH's slide, not company news. Short interest is 918k shares, about 7% of pre-issue shares and 12 days to cover on roughly 75k shares a day (FINRA 2026-10-30, per the sweep).
view: This is a roughly $40m microcap. Its price is mostly ETH held against ETH-backed debt, plus an agency, creator-tools and IP business that management says will do $150m of revenue in 2027 and that the market plainly does not believe. Monday's release has three parts. (1) Q3 revenue against about $21.3m. Q2 was $18.5m, management says about 60% of revenue falls in H2, and about 70% was booked by midyear, so a print near or slightly above consensus is plausible. There was no mid-quarter Q3 letter like the 2026-06-04 Q2 letter, and the company chose not to quote Q3 revenue at the 2026-10-26 FanEngine close, after the quarter had ended. That is weakly uninformative-to-negative. (2) The full-year line. The restatement from '$85-90m' to '$85m+ pro forma' with FanEngine contributing reads as the organic range quietly moving to its floor and being filled by an acquisition. Low end less H1 ($33m) less a $21.3m Q3 leaves a $30.7m Q4, which needs FanEngine and Peaky Blinders on top of a seasonal Q4. The street at $78.8m already sits below it, so a repeat of '$85m+ pro forma' is probably not news either way. (3) The balance sheet. Q3 will show a large fair-value gain on ETH, because ETH rose about 73% from about $1,559 to about $2,705 over the quarter; on 15,080 ETH that is about $17m. So GAAP EPS will likely print far above the -$0.16 consensus. But ETH has since fallen about 28%, so the Sep-30 NAV is stale. A subsequent-events note on margin calls, ETH sales to service the notes, or a financing would land on a name with a going-concern paragraph. The last time ETH gains drove net income positive (Q3 2025), the stock still fell 12%. Prints on this name have mostly been sold: 4 of 5. Over a Friday-close to Monday 13:00 window the weekend ETH move adds noise as large as the release itself. I lean modestly down on base rate, dilution and financing risk, and on the softened guide wording, but I cannot see the deciding line.

recommendation.reason: The lean is down: 4 of 5 prior prints sold off, the full-year guide was softened to '$85m+ pro forma' with FanEngine filling it, and a going-concern, ETH-margined balance sheet now carries a 28% ETH drawdown since quarter end, which invites a financing or margin disclosure. None of this is dated evidence that Q3 revenue or the guide lands on the wrong side of what the price assumes, and the street already sits below the guide. The weekend ETH move is undirected noise of comparable size. Confidence stays well under 65.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: Q3 revenue clearly above $21.3m (for example $24m or more) with an unqualified reaffirmation of $85-90m and no financing, ETH sale or margin-call disclosure, which on a 12-day-to-cover thin float could squeeze the stock sharply higher.

self_critique: The down-lean rests on base rate and tone, not on dated evidence about the deciding line. The street at $78.8m already prices disbelief in the guide, so a Q3 at or above $21.3m with '$85m+ pro forma' held could be read as relief. The thin float with 12 days to cover can squeeze on any good headline, including a large GAAP net-income beat that retail may read naively. The weekend ETH move, in either direction, could dominate the 13:00 ET Monday mark.
